subtopics.title: From Owner to Shareholder — the Company Form

questions.question: Limited liability means that if the company fails, a shareholder can lose:
options: Only what was paid for the shares — creditors cannot reach personal assets
Their personal assets, up to the value of the company's debts
Nothing at all under any circumstances
Only dividends already received

questions.question: The key difference between a public company (Ltd) and a private company (Pty Ltd) is that a public company:
options: Pays no income tax
May offer its shares to the public and may list on the JSE
Has no directors
Cannot borrow money

questions.question: Separation of ownership and control means:
options: Directors own the company and shareholders manage it
The auditor owns the company
Shareholders own the company but elected directors manage it — which is why an independent auditor checks the directors' stewardship
Each shareholder controls one branch of the business

questions.question: Authorised share capital is:
options: The number of shares actually sold to shareholders
The value of shares bought back
The shares held by directors only
The maximum number of shares the MOI allows the company to issue — issued shares can never exceed it

subtopics.title: Issuing Shares and Buying Them Back

questions.question: Thabiso Ltd issues 300 000 no par value shares at R6,00 each. The entry is:
options: Debit Bank R1 800 000; credit Ordinary Share Capital R1 800 000 — the full issue price goes to share capital
Debit Bank R1 800 000; credit Share Premium R600 000 and Share Capital R1 200 000
Debit Ordinary Share Capital; credit Bank R1 800 000
Debit Retained Income; credit Bank R1 800 000

questions.question: After the issue, Thabiso Ltd has 800 000 shares and share capital of R3 800 000. The average issue price per share is:
Thabiso Ltd buys back 50 000 shares at R7,00 each when the average issue price is R4,75. Retained income is debited with:
options: R112 500 — the excess of the buy-back price over the average issue price
Nothing; the full amount comes from share capital

questions.question: Shares that a company buys back are:
options: Held for resale at a later date
Transferred to the directors
Still entitled to future dividends
Cancelled — the number of shares in issue falls and they receive no future dividends

subtopics.title: Income Tax and Dividends in the Ledger

questions.question: Provisional tax payments of R350 000 were made and the final income tax for the year is R378 000. The SARS — Income Tax account shows:
options: A credit balance of R28 000 — a current liability owed to SARS
A debit balance of R28 000 — an amount receivable from SARS
A credit balance of R378 000
A nil balance

questions.question: If provisional payments had EXCEEDED the final tax assessment, the SARS balance would be:
options: A larger current liability
A current asset — a refund due to the company
Written off as an expense
Added to share capital

questions.question: The final dividend of 40 cents per share is declared after a buy-back leaves 750 000 shares in issue. The final dividend is:
options: R300 000 — computed on the 750 000 shares in issue on the declaration date

questions.question: A final dividend declared but not yet paid at year-end appears as:
options: An operating expense
Part of share capital
Income received in advance
Shareholders for dividends — a current liability settled early in the new year

subtopics.title: Loans, Directors' Fees and Audit Fees

questions.question: A loan of R500 000 at 12 percent with capitalised interest, and instalments of R110 000 paid during the year, closes at:
options: R450 000 — the loan grows by R60 000 interest before the R110 000 payments reduce it

questions.question: Capitalised interest on a loan is:
options: Not an expense because no cash was paid
Still an expense on the income statement, even though it was added to the loan rather than paid separately
Deducted from share capital
Recorded only when the loan is settled

questions.question: Directors' fees differ from dividends because directors' fees are:
options: An appropriation of profit after tax
Paid only to shareholders
An operating expense paid for the work of managing the company, deducted before net profit
Declared in cents per share

questions.question: The independent auditor is appointed by and reports to:
options: The directors, who pay the audit fee
SARS
The JSE
The shareholders — because the audit exists to check the directors' stewardship of the shareholders' money

subtopics.title: The Spaza That Became a Company

questions.question: Why are strangers willing to buy shares in a business they will never manage?
options: Limited liability — the most they can lose is what they paid for their shares
They are guaranteed a fixed monthly wage
They automatically become directors
The company must refund them on demand

questions.question: In the cake picture, authorised share capital is the cake tin and issued share capital is:
options: The icing on the cake
How much cake has actually been cut and sold
The recipe in the rulebook
The cake the directors keep

questions.question: The company's rulebook, registered when the company is formed, is called:
options: The audit report
The share certificate
The Memorandum of Incorporation
The appropriation account

questions.question: The central tension of the company form is that:
options: Shareholders must work in the business
Companies may not borrow money
Directors always own all the shares
The people spending the money are not the people who own it — which is why an outside auditor checks the books

questions.question: Why do the new shares sell at R6,00 when earlier shares averaged R4,00?
options: The business is worth more now — a slice of a bigger cake costs more
The law requires every new issue to be at a higher price
The bank sets the share price
Old shareholders are refunded the difference

questions.question: In the buy-back of 50 000 shares at R7,00, the R350 000 paid out is split as:
options: All R350 000 from retained income
R237 500 from share capital at the average issue price, and R112 500 from retained income
All R350 000 from share capital
R175 000 from each account

questions.question: The parting-bonus part of the buy-back price comes from retained income because:
options: Retained income belongs to SARS
The bank insists on it
The capital account only ever received the average issue price per share — the extra is a distribution of past profits
Share capital may never be reduced

questions.question: After the buy-back, each remaining share is:
options: Worth exactly what it was before
Entitled to a refund
Converted into a loan to the company
A slightly bigger fraction of the company, because the cake is now cut into fewer slices

questions.question: The company paid provisional tax of R350 000 and the final tax came to R378 000. At year-end the company:
options: Still owes SARS R28 000, shown as a debt on the balance sheet
Is owed R28 000 by SARS
Owes SARS the full R378 000
Owes nothing because provisional tax settles everything

questions.question: Why is a dividend not really a bill the company owes automatically?
options: Because dividends are paid by SARS
Because no shareholder can demand one — the directors must declare it first
Because dividends are always zero
Because only employees receive dividends

questions.question: The interim dividend was R200 000 and the final dividend R300 000, on different share counts, because:
options: The dividend rate halved during the year
The company issued more shares before the final dividend
The buy-back reduced the shares in issue to 750 000 before the final dividend was declared
Interim dividends are always smaller by law

questions.question: A director who also owns shares is paid through two different doors:
options: Salary and wages
Audit fees and interest
Rent and commission
Directors' fees for the work of managing, and dividends for the shares owned
